messages.body: Narrow the channel. Once the dykes stand, the current carries the silt away for good. Diversion lets the bed silt up, and within ten years it breaks again.
Diversion is cheaper and works this year. Narrowing costs twice as much; I doubt we can pay for it.
Earlier reigns tried diversion again and again, and it failed every time. Narrowing needs strict checks on the dykes to stop corner-cutting.
@Works @Revenue You disagree. Works says diversion breaks again in ten years; Revenue says there isn't silver for narrowing. Answer each other.
@Works Narrowing is costed at 800,000 taels. Revenue can release 400,000 at most this year. Where does the rest come from?
@Revenue Diversion saves this year's silver. When it breaks again in ten years, closing it will cost far more than 800,000. Under Jiajing we diverted three times, and it broke three times.
@Revenue The Jiajing cases Works cites are accurate. Whatever diversion saves now will be repaid twice over.
@Works Revenue has only 400,000 taels this year. Can narrowing wait a step, so we do what's urgent this year first?

We can give ground: this year close the breach and build the inner dykes for 240,000 taels; the outer dykes next year. Add spillway dams at the dangerous stretches to release floods, which takes the best of diversion.
At 240,000 taels this year, Revenue can pay. We'll raise next year's dyke silver separately. Agreed.
The compromise works; no new objections. With the dykes built over two years, corner-cutting is likeliest in the second, so the inspection should check the dykes specifically.

process.note: Consensus: Narrow the channel; close the breach and build the inner dykes this year, the outer dykes next year, spillway dams at dangerous stretches; cost spread over two years; disagreements: No real disagreement once Works gave ground; the Censorate asks for a dedicated dyke inspection
In vermilion: as proposed. Narrow the channel, build the dykes over two years, spillway dams at the dangerous stretches → D001

messages.body: In favour: both provinces in parallel, done in three months.
In favour, but watch for unrest in Jiangnan.
Against the plan as it stands: every figure comes from local officials with no independent check, so there will be forgeries. Add a stage for the censors to verify.
How will Revenue verify what the localities report?
@Revenue How do you answer the Censorate?
Agreed to add verification; it can come after the pilot.
Acceptable, provided verification comes after the pilot and before rollout.
@Revenue @Censorate How should it be verified? Resurveying whole counties takes too long, but no check at all isn't safe.
Spot-survey a tenth of the land in each county against the register; if the error exceeds two per cent, resurvey the whole county.
I accept a ten per cent spot survey with a full resurvey above two per cent. The censors choose the plots at short notice, so the localities can't know in advance.
Agreed; the censors choose the plots.

messages.body: Open the markets. Trade instead of war, and the frontier armies can save thirty per cent of their pay.
Agreed: the horse markets bring in tax silver and frontier pay can come down.
Against: this is raising a tiger. If he breaks faith, our defences will already have slackened, and regret will come too late.
@Works If the markets stay closed, how much of the Xuanda wall needs repair, and at what cost?
Three hundred li of the Xuanda wall need repair: 600,000 taels over three years. With the markets open, most of it can wait; patching the fifty most exposed li costs 100,000.
@War If Altan Khan breaks faith after the markets open, and the wall repairs have been put off, what holds him back?
@War Revise the market proposal in light of Works' numbers and the Censorate's question, then resubmit.

Revised: no more than 10,000 horses a year; if he breaks faith the markets close and the frontier armies return to full pay that day; patch the fifty most exposed li of wall now rather than deferring it all.
@Revenue Work out the tax silver and the pay saved under War's revised plan.

10,000 horses a year yields about 40,000 taels in tax; thirty per cent off frontier pay saves about 300,000 a year; the 100,000 for the wall is paid once. Over three years that's a net saving of roughly 800,000 taels.
The cap and the closure clause are acceptable. I still dissent: please record my objection verbatim in the memorial and review it in three years.
Your servant fears the frontier generals have long traded privately; the horse numbers War reports may not be reliable.
